source: Curated feed — records gathered from official program pages

records.title: StudentCam
records.description: C-SPAN's national video documentary contest. You make a short film about an issue that affects your community or the country.

participation.howToJoin: Enter alone or with a team of 2 or 3 students.

records.title: Congressional Art Competition
records.description: Visual art contest run in each congressional district every spring. You enter through your own member of Congress's office.

records.title: President's Environmental Youth Award (PEYA)
records.description: National EPA award for a student-led environmental project you have already done in your community. Grades 6-12 compete in one category.

participation.howToJoin: Apply alone or as a group of students.

records.title: Youth Conservation Corps (YCC)
records.description: Paid summer job on a crew in a national park, doing needed work on public lands. Open to U.S. permanent residents ages 15 to 18.

records.title: Poetry Out Loud
records.org: National Endowment for the Arts & Poetry Foundation
records.description: National poetry recitation contest. You memorize and perform poems, starting at your school and moving up to state and national finals. Your school must be registered with the state coordinator.

participation.howToJoin: Compete through a school or organization registered with your state coordinator.

records.title: Princeton University Mathematics Competition (PUMaC)
records.description: Student-run math contest at Princeton. Teams come from high schools or well-defined regions.

participation.howToJoin: Compete on a team from your high school or region.

records.title: √mathroots
records.description: Free residential summer math program at MIT for current high school students. There is no tuition or housing cost.

records.title: Hampshire College Summer Studies in Mathematics (HCSSiM)
records.description: Intensive residential summer math program. The 2026 session cost $7,208.

records.title: MathILy
records.description: Intensive residential summer math program for strong math students. Tuition is charged.

records.title: Wharton High School Data Science Competition
records.org: Wharton Global Youth Program, University of Pennsylvania
records.description: Free sports analytics contest from Wharton. You use real data to answer a sports question.

records.title: Wharton Moneyball Academy
records.org: Wharton Global Youth Program, University of Pennsylvania
records.description: Summer program at Wharton where rising juniors and seniors study sports analytics. Tuition is charged.

records.title: UCSC Scholar Immersion Program (SIP)
records.description: Summer research with UC Santa Cruz mentors on open-ended projects. The SIP 2027 application fee is $68, and fee waivers are available.

records.title: The Junior Academy
records.org: The New York Academy of Sciences
records.description: Free online program where you join an international team and work with STEM experts on real-world challenges.

records.title: Bennington Young Writers Awards
records.description: Free writing contest for poetry, fiction, and nonfiction, now part of the Bennington Young Creators Awards.

records.title: National Security Language Initiative for Youth (NSLI-Y)
records.description: Merit-based scholarship for high school students to study a critical language, either abroad or online.

records.title: Congress-Bundestag Youth Exchange (CBYX)
records.org: U.S. Department of State & German Bundestag
records.description: Scholarship to live with a host family in Germany and attend a German high school. No previous German is required.

records.title: Solar Car Challenge
records.description: Teams of high school students learn to build a roadworthy solar car, then take part in the Challenge.

participation.howToJoin: Build and race the car as a high school team.

records.title: NASA HUNCH
records.description: Classes at participating schools design and build real products for NASA. You take part through your school.

records.title: VFW Voice of Democracy
records.description: Audio essay contest on a patriotic theme. You record your essay and enter through a local VFW post, with scholarships at each level.

records.title: Optimist International Essay Contest
records.description: Essay contest run by local Optimist Clubs. Club winners move up to district contests, which award college scholarships.

records.title: Optimist International Oratorical Contest
records.description: Speech contest run by local Optimist Clubs, with college scholarships at the district level.

records.title: Habitat for Humanity Youth Programs
records.description: Volunteer with Habitat for Humanity through its youth programs and help build homes near you.

records.title: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program
records.org: Civil Air Patrol (U.S. Air Force Auxiliary)
records.description: Join a local Civil Air Patrol squadron to learn aviation and leadership. Annual dues are $25 to $50.

records.title: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
records.org: NYC Department of Youth & Community Development
records.description: Paid summer work and career exploration for New York City youth ages 14 to 24.

records.title: One Summer Chicago
records.description: Chicago's summer jobs, internships, and training for youth ages 14 to 24, with city agencies, companies, and community groups.

records.title: AEOP Internships and Fellowships
records.description: Paid research internships in Army research labs and partner university labs. Positions are competitive.

records.title: Gains in the Education of Mathematics and Science (GEMS)
records.description: Summer STEM camp at Army research sites. There is no fee, and students get a small stipend.

records.title: NIST Summer High School Intern Program (SHIP)
records.org: National Institute of Standards and Technology
records.description: Seven-week unpaid research internship with NIST scientists. You must be a U.S. citizen with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA.

records.title: Stockholm Junior Water Prize (U.S.)
records.description: Science fair-style contest for water research projects. State winners go on to the national competition.

records.title: JA Company Program
records.description: Start and run a real student company with classmates through Junior Achievement.

records.title: JA Titan
records.description: Junior Achievement business simulation where you make decisions to run a company.

records.title: Essentially Ellington
records.description: Free Jazz at Lincoln Center program for high school jazz bands. Your school band takes part as a group.

participation.howToJoin: Take part as a high school jazz band.

records.title: Grammy Camp
records.description: Summer music industry camp in cities such as Nashville, Miami, and New York. Tuition runs $2,500 to $3,600 by location.

records.title: Young Entrepreneurs Academy (YEA!)
records.description: Class run by local YEA! chapters where you build a real business. Top students compete for college scholarships and start-up money.

records.title: Polyphony Lit
records.description: Online literary magazine for high school writers. Submit your writing, or join the student editorial staff to review other teens' work.

records.title: Girl Scout Gold Award
records.description: The top Girl Scout award for a lasting community project you lead. You must be a registered Senior or Ambassador Girl Scout.

records.title: Elks Most Valuable Student Scholarship
records.description: College scholarship for U.S. citizen seniors, from $1,000 to $7,500 a year. The top 20 scholars receive $30,000.

records.title: Cooke College Scholarship Program
records.description: Large college scholarship for high-achieving seniors with financial need. Each award covers much of tuition, living costs, books, and fees.

records.title: Ron Brown Scholar Program
records.description: $40,000 college scholarships for African American seniors with strong academics, leadership, and community service. The 2027 application is open.

records.title: QuestBridge National College Match
records.description: College admission and scholarship process that matches high-achieving seniors from low-income backgrounds with full four-year scholarships at 55 partner colleges.

records.title: PYNtern Program
records.description: Paid work-based learning in Philadelphia. Rising 9th and 10th graders start with career exploration, and older teens move into internships.

records.title: Whitney Youth Insights
records.description: After-school and summer program at the Whitney where New York City teens work with contemporary artists.

records.title: InvestWrite
records.description: National essay contest about investing. It is open only to students in The Stock Market Game, so your teacher must run it.

participation.howToJoin: Your Stock Market Game teacher submits the best essays.

records.title: National Personal Finance Challenge
records.description: Nationwide contest on earning, spending, saving, investing, and credit. Teams with a coach compete at state and national levels.

participation.howToJoin: Compete on a team with a coach.

records.title: Summer High School Advanced Research Program (SHARP)
records.description: Summer research program at the University of Nebraska Medical Center for high school sophomores and juniors. For U.S. citizens and permanent residents, with a 3.0 GPA, a completed science course, and two recommendation letters considered.

records.title: Summer Engineering Seminar (SES)
records.org: Santa Clara University School of Engineering
records.description: Free five-day residential engineering seminar at Santa Clara University for high school sophomores and juniors, with priority for sophomores. Housing and meals cost nothing, and applicants are judged on math and science grades and financial need. The 2027 application opens in December.

records.title: Cooper Union Summer STEM
records.description: Three- or six-week college-level engineering and computer science classes at Cooper Union in New York City. Financial aid is available, with priority for NYC residents. Applications for 2027 open December 11, 2026.

records.title: Flight Teen Volunteers
records.description: Teens ages 14 to 18 run aviation and STEM activities for museum visitors in San Carlos, including the Invention Lab and virtual reality experiences. Applications are taken on an ongoing basis.

records.title: Cedars-Sinai Teen Volunteer Program
records.description: Session-based hospital volunteering in Los Angeles where teens work alongside patients and staff. You must be 14 to 18 and complete a full session. The volunteer jacket costs $30.

records.title: Tar Heel Business Academy
records.description: One-week business courses taught by Kenan-Flagler professors in Charlotte and Chapel Hill, including Business Essentials, Business of Sports, and Entrepreneurship. The fee is $2,995 and a need-based scholarship can be requested. Apply by the November 16 priority deadline.

records.title: Northeastern Young Scholars Program (YSP)
records.org: Northeastern University Center for STEM Education
records.description: Free six-week research placement in Northeastern labs in engineering, science, and health sciences for Massachusetts juniors. Students must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents and live within commuting distance of Boston.

records.title: High School Investor Challenge
records.description: Pre-college finance program where students manage a $100,000 virtual portfolio and learn securities analysis and portfolio management. The 2027 application has not opened yet.

records.title: CMU CS Scholars
records.description: Fully funded four-week residential computer science program at Carnegie Mellon for 10th graders. Open to U.S. citizens and permanent residents, and documentation of financial need is required to apply.

records.title: CMU AI Scholars
records.description: Fully funded four-week residential AI program at Carnegie Mellon for 11th graders, with research projects and faculty lectures. Open to U.S. citizens and permanent residents, and documentation of financial need is required to apply.

records.title: Spirit of America Youth Leadership
records.description: Four-day residential civics and leadership program at Valley Forge with a free enterprise team challenge. The fee is $850, and many students attend free thanks to donor support. Sessions run from October 2026 through July 2027.

records.title: NASA TechRise Student Challenge
records.description: School teams design an experiment that NASA flies on a high-altitude test vehicle in summer 2027. A teacher or school employee submits the team's proposal, and 60 winning teams are chosen.

participation.howToJoin: A teacher or school employee forms the team and submits the proposal.

records.title: Dream with Us High School Engineering Challenge
records.description: Teams of 3 to 7 students design a new cargo aircraft and write a proposal for it. Registration closes December 8, 2026, and the engineering notebook is due January 25, 2027.

records.title: High School Entrepreneurship and AI Video Pitch Competition
records.org: Stevens Institute of Technology School of Business
records.description: Pitch a business idea in a short video. Entries are individual, the registration fee is $25, and prizes are $500, $250, and $100. Register by January 8, 2027 and submit the video by January 15.

records.title: Global Stock Pitch Competition
records.description: Students pick a public company and build their best stock idea, alone or in teams of two, then pitch it. The fee is $30 per person, registration opens December 15, 2026, and finalists attend the Global Youth Investment Summit.

records.title: Magee-Womens HS Summer Research Internship
records.description: Six-week biomedical research internship in Pittsburgh where each student runs their own project with an investigator. Students must be over 16, and a $1,800 stipend is available to students from households that qualify. Applications for 2027 open in late fall 2026.

records.title: Van Andel Institute HS Graduate Research Program
records.description: Eight-week paid lab research program for graduating high school seniors, working full time with scientists on cell biology, genetics, neuroscience, and more. It pays $15 an hour and has 10 spots. U.S. citizens and permanent residents only. Applications run January to mid-March 2027.

records.title: Pathways Research Explorers (High School Explorers Program)
records.description: Two-week introduction to cancer research at Fred Hutch in Seattle, with hands-on lab activities. It costs nothing to attend, students who finish get a $500 award, and applicants must live in the Seattle area. Applications for 2027 open next January.

records.title: Summer Environmental Interns
records.description: Five-day wetland science service internship at Tule Ponds in Fremont, with water sampling, plant surveys, and microbe studies. It is free, and 10 to 15 students are chosen. Applications for 2027 are due April 15.

records.title: Children's Health Council Teen Volunteers
records.description: Teens ages 14 to 18 volunteer with a Palo Alto nonprofit that supports children and teens with learning differences and mental health needs. Volunteers serve across the Peninsula and South Bay.

records.title: TAG-Ed High School Summer Internship
records.org: TAG-Ed (Technology Association of Georgia Education Collaborative)
records.description: Eight-week summer STEM internship in Georgia where interns are matched with host companies and work in pairs on a defined project. Paid and unpaid placements exist, and students must be 17 by June 1 and able to work in the U.S.

records.title: GENIUS Olympiad
records.org: Terra Science and Education (hosted by St. John Fisher University)
records.description: International project competition on environmental topics, with tracks including AI, robotics, and science. Applications open in December 2026, cost $75 per project, and finalists present at St. John Fisher University in Rochester, New York in June 2027.

records.title: Neuroscience High School Scholars Program
records.org: UCLA Mary S. Easton Center for Alzheimer's Research and Care
records.description: Free virtual summer neuroscience program from UCLA for rising juniors and seniors, with a focus on students at schools with limited access to neuroscience courses. Dates and the application deadline will be posted in December 2026.

records.title: Babson Summer Study
records.description: Three-week program for rising juniors and seniors on building an entrepreneurial mindset, offered online or in person in 2027. There is a $100 application fee, waived for students applying for need-based aid.

records.title: Computer History Museum Teen Volunteer Interns
records.description: Students in grades 9 to 12 research technology history and run tours and hands-on activities for young visitors at the museum in Mountain View.

records.title: IBM SkillsBuild for High School Students
records.description: Free self-paced online courses on AI literacy, ethics of generative AI, and other tech skills for students ages 13 to 18. Start any time.

records.title: Elements of AI
records.description: Free online introduction to artificial intelligence that needs no coding experience. It covers what AI can and can't do and how to start building simple AI methods. Start any time.

records.title: Code in Place
records.description: Free online course that teaches the first half of Stanford's intro Python class (CS106A) to beginners. Each group of 10 students gets a volunteer teacher. Sessions run in cohorts, so check the site for the next one.
